arxiv-2103-10837.title: Quantum machine learning of graph-structured data
arxiv-2103-10837.creator: Kerstin Beer, Megha Khosla, Julius Köhler, Tobias J. Osborne
arxiv-2103-10837.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kerstin Beer, Megha Khosla, Julius Köhler, Tobias J. Osborne. Graph structures are ubiquitous throughout the natural sciences. Here we consider graph-structured quantum data and describe how to carry out its quantum machine learning via quantum neural networks . In particular, we consider training data in the form of pairs of input and output quantum states associated with the vertices of a graph, together with edges encoding correlations between the vertices.

arxiv-2211-02111.title: Translated Skip Connections - Expanding the Receptive Fields of Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2211-02111.creator: J. Bruton, H. Wang
arxiv-2211-02111.description: Abstract The effective receptive field of a fully convolutional neural network is an important consideration when designing an architecture, as it defines the portion of the input visible to each convolutional kernel. We propose a neural network module, extending traditional skip connections, called the translated skip connection.

arxiv-2310-10152.title: Entropy for Monge–Ampère Measures in the Prescribed Singularities Setting This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Differential Geometry Inspired by Mathematical Physics in honor of Jean-Pierre Bourguignon for his 75th birthday. arxiv-2310-10152.description: Abstract In this note, we generalize the notion of entropy for potentials in a relative full Monge–Ampère mass ℰ ⁡ ( X , θ , ϕ ) \mathcal{E}(X,\theta,\phi) , for a model potential ϕ \phi . We then investigate stability properties of this condition with respect to blow-ups and perturbation of the cohomology class.

arxiv-2403-11800.title: Loop Special Relativity: Kaluza-Klein area metric as a line element for stringy events
arxiv-2403-11800.creator: Aharon Davidson, Nadav Barkai
arxiv-2403-11800.description: Abstract Let a physical event constitute a simple loop in spacetime. This in turn calls for a generalized loop line element (= distance 2 between two neighboring loops) capable of restoring, at the shrinking loop limit, the special relativistic line element (= distance 2 between the two neighboring center-of-masses, respectively).

arxiv-2502-01311.title: TFBS-Finder: Deep Learning-based Model with DNABERT and Convolutional Networks to Predict Transcription Factor Binding Sites
arxiv-2502-01311.creator: Nimisha Ghosh, Pratik Dutta, and Daniele Santoni
arxiv-2502-01311.description: Abstract Transcription factors are proteins that regulate the expression of genes by binding to specific genomic regions known as Transcription Factor Binding Sites (TFBSs), typically located in the promoter regions of those genes. Accurate prediction of these binding sites is essential for understanding the complex gene regulatory networks underlying various cellular functions.

arxiv-2510-23710.title: Tailoring Superconductivity with Two-Level Systems
arxiv-2510-23710.creator: Joshuah T. Heath, Alexander C. Tyner, S. Pamir Alpay, Peter Krogstrup, Alexander V. Balatsky
arxiv-2510-23710.description: Abstract We investigate the impact of two-level systems (TLSs) on superconductivity, treating them as soft modes localised in real space. We show that these defects can either enhance or suppress the superconducting critical temperature, depending on their surface density and average frequency.

pmc-10673081.title: Solution Combustion Synthesis of Ni-Based Nanocatalyst Using Ethylenediaminetetraacetic Acid and Nickel-Carbon Nanotube Growth Behavior
pmc-10673081.creator: Juyoung Kim, Hwanseok Lee, Jaekwang Lee, Hyunjo Yoo, Ilguk Jo, Heesoo Lee
pmc-10673081.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We studied the influence of the ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) content used as combustion fuel when fabricating nickel oxide (NiO) nanocatalysts via solution combustion synthesis, as well as the growth behavior of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) using this catalyst. Nickel nitrate hexahydrate (Ni(NO3)2∙6H2O) was used as the metal precursor (an oxidizer), and the catalysts were synthesized by adjusting the molar ratio of fuel (EDTA) to oxidizer in the range of 1:0.25 to 2.0.

pmc-12615973.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in lung cancer: a case series
pmc-12615973.creator: Abdul Wali Khan, Simran Chandra, Himil Mahadevia, Janakiraman Subramanian, Ben Ponvilawan, Dhruv Bansal
pmc-12615973.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are established treatments for various malignancies, including lung, kidney, and colorectal cancers. However, their broad use has led to an increase in immune-related adverse events (irAEs), with thyroiditis, colitis, and pneumonitis being the most common. Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a rare but severe irAE characterized by excessive immune activation, leading to systemic inflammation and multi-organ dysfunction.

pmc-13097420.title: Impact of early dexmedetomidine administration on short‐ and long‐term outcomes in critically traumatic brain injury patients: A retrospective study using the MIMIC‐IV database
pmc-13097420.creator: Yang Long, Long‐Zhen Liu, Xiao‐Xue Tan, Yong‐Hu Zhang, Cheng‐Xi Liu, Shan Liu, Wen‐Jie Liu
pmc-13097420.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Traumatic brain injury (TBI) causes significant mortality. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) shows neuroprotective potential in animals, but clinical evidence remains inconsistent. We evaluated the impact of early DEX, initiated within 48 h of admission with a treatment duration of at least 4 h, on survival in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with TBI using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care‐IV (MIMIC‐IV) database. Outcomes included 28‐day, hospital, and 1‐year mortality, analyzed via propensity score matching (PSM), multivariable Cox models, and subgroup analyses.

pmc-13408107.creator: Yiyin Qiu, Jianjun Chen, Yan Fan, Md Rakib Hossain, Fei Wang, Xibei Yang
pmc-13408107.description: The degraded regions of ancient murals often contain intricate textures and structural curves, presenting major challenges for traditional mural restoration. Although digital image inpainting offers a viable approach, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based methods are commonly constrained by these complex scenarios and struggle with global consistency due to their limited receptive fields.

pmc-13660370.title: Hierarchical clustering for disentangling population vulnerability to asthma
pmc-13660370.creator: Xiang Gao, Parvathinathan Venkitasubramaniam, Hyunok Choi
pmc-13660370.description: Asthma is influenced by air pollution and weather conditions, yet asthma-related responses to these exposures may vary across communities due to heterogeneity in population vulnerability—defined here as a context represented by socioeconomic, demographic, and landscape conditions. We propose a clustering framework to characterize region-level population vulnerability prior to exposure–asthma modeling.
